claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 conventionally requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Spark plasma sintering can densify single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 2000 °C.
SPS at approximately 2000 °C will reduce pore formation relative to conventional sintering above 2300 °C.
Reduced pore formation will limit subsequent hole formation during long-term liquid plating bath exposure.
SPS is proposed as the sole processing intervention.
The proposed SPS treatment uses approximately 2000 °C, pressure, a controlled dwell time, and an inert atmosphere.
Rapid heating and pulsed current during SPS enhance densification and markedly reduce grain-boundary porosity.
SPS facilitates rapid densification while limiting prolonged high-temperature exposure.
Lower processing temperature and shorter sintering duration reduce defect sites.
Pores and other defect sites initiate holes during liquid plating bath exposure.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable to or better than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will contain fewer pores than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will resist degradation during prolonged liquid plating bath exposure better than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically retains relatively high porosity and microstructural defects.
Porosity and microstructural defects in conventionally sintered ZrB2 accelerate component failure under liquid plating conditions.
The hypothesis is limited to SPS conditions that preserve single-phase ZrB2 without introducing secondary phases.
Uniform SPS microstructures and phase purity may not be maintained across larger samples or different SPS configurations.
